scope: Filtering or grouping patients by sex
description: Sex is coded 'M' for male and 'F' for female. Thirteen of 1238 rows are blank and mean unknown, not a third category; exclude them rather than treating them as a value.

scope: Any question asking for patient age or filtering by age
description: Age is not stored. Compute it as the current calendar year minus the year of birth taken from the birthday column. Because it uses the current date, the same patient's computed age changes over time. Patients with a null birthday have no computable age.

scope: Comparing inpatient and outpatient groups
description: The patient status column stores '+' for inpatient and '-' for outpatient. Blank values (34 rows) are unknown and '+(' (3 rows) is an inpatient variant; treat blank as unknown rather than as a separate group.

scope: Filtering patients by a named disease or counting disease frequency
description: Diagnosis labels are free text. A single patient may carry several diseases in one comma-separated label (for example 'SLE, SJS'), labels may end with 'susp' for suspected disease, and case/encoding varies between tables ('SJS' in tab02 versus 'SjS' in tab01). Exact equality on one label therefore excludes combined entries; substring or label-splitting is needed when the question refers to a disease that may co-occur.

scope: Choosing between patient-level and examination-level diagnosis
description: tab02.fld008 holds one consolidated diagnosis per patient and covers all 1238 patients (1 blank). tab01.fld008 holds a diagnosis per examination, is null in 331 of 806 rows, and only resolves to a patient for 69 distinct patient IDs. Use the patient-level column when counting patients by disease; use the examination-level column only when the question is about a specific visit.

scope: Counting patients or averaging values across laboratory panels
description: tab03 stores one row per patient per test date, so a patient contributes many rows (1 to 226 panels, mean 46.1). Joining patient attributes to lab rows multiplies rows; count distinct patient identifiers when the question asks how many patients, and decide explicitly whether a value-level filter (for example any panel above a cutoff) or an aggregate is intended.

scope: Any analysis that joins examination records to patients or laboratory panels
description: Only 69 of the 763 distinct patient identifiers in tab01 also exist in tab02, and only 20 exist in tab03; 70 of 806 examination rows join to a patient record. In addition, 36 examination rows have a null patient identifier and six patient/date pairs appear twice. Questions that combine examination attributes with patient or laboratory data therefore operate on a small intersection; report the intersection rather than assuming full coverage.

scope: All date columns in tab01, tab02 and tab03
description: Dates are stored as ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' text, so range comparison works lexicographically and year filters can use the first four characters. Laboratory dates span 1981-01-27 to 1999-03-04 and examination dates 1989-04-18 to 1998-04-17.

scope: Interpreting glucose as normal or abnormal
description: A glucose value is treated as not within the normal range when it is at or above 180; values below 180 are within the normal range. Observed values span 62 to 499, with 129 of 1705 measurements at or above 180.

scope: Interpreting total cholesterol as normal or high
description: Total cholesterol is high when at or above 250 and within the normal range when below 250. Observed values span 37 to 568, with 1545 of 10664 measurements at or above 250.

scope: Interpreting CPK as normal or abnormal
description: CPK is within the normal range when below 250 and beyond the normal range when at or above 250. Observed values span 0 to 10835, with 288 of 5016 measurements at or above 250.

scope: Interpreting GPT/ALT as normal or elevated
description: The upper limit used in this workload is 60 U/L: values at or above 60 exceed the normal range. A question may state its own numeric cutoff (for example greater than 30), which then replaces the general upper limit. Observed values span 1 to 4780, with 890 of 11274 measurements at or above 60.

scope: Interpreting creatinine as normal or abnormal
description: Creatinine is abnormal when at or above 1.5. Observed values span 0.1 to 17.1, with 361 of 11253 measurements at or above 1.5.

scope: Interpreting the urea nitrogen borderline value
description: The workload treats the value 29 as 'just within the borderline of passing' for urea nitrogen. Observed values span 0 to 152 and 44 measurements equal exactly 29.

scope: Comparing albumin values
description: Albumin is expressed in g/dL over the observed range 1.0 to 5.8. A question may state its own cutoff (for example ALB less than 4); 3287 of 11068 measurements are below 4. Do not confuse albumin with the adjacent total protein column, which has a different range.

scope: Interpreting IgG as normal or abnormal
description: IgG is normal when strictly above 900 and strictly below 2000. Observed values span 3 to 6510, and 1764 of 2680 measurements fall inside that open interval.

scope: Interpreting IgM as normal or abnormal
description: IgM is normal between 40 and 400 inclusive; it is abnormal when at or below 40 or at or above 400. Observed values span 0 to 1573, with 208 of 2678 measurements abnormal.

scope: Interpreting anti-Scl70 results
description: Anti-Scl70 values are text. 'negative' and '0' mean a negative (normal) result; numeric strings such as '1', '4' or '16' are positive titers. The column never contains '-' or '+-'. Null means the test was not performed.

scope: Interpreting anti-SSB results
description: Anti-SSB values are text. 'negative' and '0' mean a negative (normal) result; numeric strings such as '1', '2', '8' or '32' are positive titers. The column never contains '-' or '+-'. Null means the test was not performed.

scope: Interpreting anti-centromere results
description: Anti-centromere values are text. 'negative' and '0' mean a negative (normal) result; the column contains only these two values among 15 non-null results. The column never contains '-' or '+-', so filters written with those codes match nothing. Null means the test was not performed.

scope: Interpreting CRP as abnormal
description: CRP is abnormal when the qualitative result is '+'. Normal or negative results appear as '-' or as thresholds such as '<0.2' and '<0.3'; numeric strings such as '0.6' are quantitative values. The same column mixes all three encodings, so compare against the exact stored string used by the question.

scope: Filtering on thrombosis level
description: Thrombosis level is an integer from 0 to 3 where 0 means no recorded thrombosis and higher values mean increasing degree. Distribution: 0=726, 1=57, 2=18, 3=5 examination records.

scope: Interpreting coagulation-related examination flags
description: Three adjacent examination columns (fld009, fld010, fld011) hold '+', '-' or null. '+' means the finding is present, '-' means absent, and null means not recorded. A 'positive degree of coagulation' is satisfied when any of the three columns is '+'. 75 examination rows and 74 distinct patients satisfy this.

scope: Determining whether a patient has symptoms
description: Symptoms are recorded as free text in tab01.fld012. A non-null value means symptoms were recorded; a null value means no symptom was recorded. Only 80 of 806 examination rows carry a symptom text, and the column exists only at examination level, so patient-level linkage is limited by the examination join coverage.

scope: Filtering examinations by ANA pattern
description: ANA pattern is a categorical string of one or more letter codes (S, P, D, N) joined by commas or dots, with occasional lowercase. 'Only S' means the stored pattern is exactly 'S', not a combination such as 'P,S' or 'S,P'. The dominant values are 'S'=252, 'P'=178 and 'P,S'=89.

scope: Interpreting ANA titer values
description: ANA titer is numeric with observed values 0, 4, 16, 64, 256, 1024 and 4096; 0 means not detected. A titer can be present while the pattern is null (223 rows), but no pattern exists without a titer.

scope: Selecting the anti-cardiolipin column
description: Two numeric examination columns hold anti-cardiolipin: fld003 (IgG isotype, range 0.0-2150.3) and fld004 (IgM isotype, range 0.0-187122.0, one extreme outlier). Workload reference text is internally inconsistent, sometimes naming the immunoglobulin M laboratory column instead, so the isotype named in the question must decide the column.

scope: Comparing platelet counts
description: Platelet counts are integers from 5 to 5844. The workload uses a threshold of 400 for elevated platelets; 875 of 11287 measurements exceed 400.

scope: Interpreting laboratory panels
description: Laboratory coverage is sparse and uneven: 1012 of 13908 panels have all main analytes null, glucose is present on 1705 panels, IgG on 2680 and anti-Scl70 on only 28. Comparisons apply only to non-null values; null must not be treated as normal or as zero. One column (fld061) is empty in all 13908 rows.

scope: Questions referring to whether patient-level data was recorded
description: tab02.fld016 is a patient-level date present for 1022 of 1238 patients. The workload uses a null value to mean 'data not recorded'. Its clinical meaning (death, discharge or last contact) cannot be established from the data: it is after fld017 for 870 of 882 patients with both dates, but laboratory panels fall after it for 100 of 244 patients.
